neutral_facts.value: The prosecution alleges that a group of individuals conspired to kill an RSS member, resulting in his death. The incident occurred on 16th October 2016 when the victim was attacked with a sharp-edged weapon and killed. The accused, including the appellant, were arrested and investigated by the National Investigation Agency (NIA). The investigation revealed that the accused were members of a group involved in previous killings of RSS members. There were frequent communications among the accused prior to and after the incident, and evidence such as a banner with their names and photographs, call records, and a letter detailing past murders were recovered. The trial court and High Court found sufficient grounds to proceed with the case, concluding that a prima facie case of conspiracy and murder was made out.

quotes.text: The application was dismissed by the trial Judge/Special Judge who ordered for framing of charges against him for the aforesaid offences under Order dated 2 nd January, 2018 came to be challenged by the appellant in a writ petition filed under Article 226 and 227 of Constitution of India read with Section 482 CrPC which was dismissed by a lucid impugned judgment dated 22 nd November, 2018 which is a subject matter of challenge in the instant appeal.

prosecution_argument.value: The prosecution argued that there was sufficient material to establish a prima facie case of conspiracy among the accused persons, including the appellant, and that the trial court correctly framed charges against the appellant based on the evidence and the charge sheet.

quotes.text: The series of evidence reveals the appellant’s involvement in the commission of crime:- i) Appellant is the District President of the Popular Front of India(PFI) which has been involved in killings of several RSS members/Hindu leaders in Karnataka in the past three years.

defence_argument.value: The defence argued that there was no material against the appellant, the charge against him was based on mere suspicion, and the High Court's judgment was erroneous and led to a miscarriage of justice.

quotes.text: The charge against the appellant is without any basis and merely on suspicion as there is nothing to reveal that the appellant was the main conspirator behind the alleged murder termed as a terror attack.

legal_principle_applied.value: The Supreme Court applied the legal principle that the trial court has the power to sift and weigh evidence to determine whether a prima facie case has been made out against the accused, and that grave suspicion, not mere suspicion, justifies framing of charges.

quotes.text: The Judge while considering the question of framing charge under Section 227 CrPC in sessions cases (which is akin to Section 239 CrPC pertaining to warrant cases) has the undoubted power to sift and weigh the evidence for the limited purpose of finding out whether or not a prima facie case against the accused has been made out.
